Dacca, Friday Morning The Day You Begin Weather: Haze, Smoke
From the National Assembly . By Wire

Conduct Bill Passed In Midnight Sitting

Sweeping speech law clears the House after one o'clock, with barely an hour of debate. Editors ask what it means for the page you are reading.
The empty press gallery, photographed at a quarter past one this morning.

The House rose past midnight to pass a law widening the penalties for what may be said online, handing regulators new powers to order material removed. Members voted with the chamber half empty and the public benches cleared.

Rights groups, awake and unhappy, warned of a chilling effect on ordinary speech and on the press. Supporters of the bill called it a measure for public order. Few outside the chamber had seen the final text.

What the law will mean in practice, for a reporter, an editor, or a reader, is the question every desk in the city is now asking. It is also, as it happens, the first thing you will learn to weigh.
